0f33cbad999b81f446858b93d6343deccd1d481a.summary: Yoroi Malware ZLab describes attackers delivering malware through XLL files, Excel add-in binaries that load in one click, starting in mid-2021. Samples in the report drop AgentTesla, Formbook and Dridex, with payloads fetched from Discord CDN and injected via process hollowing. The report describes campaigns against manufacturing companies in Italy and frames the trend as a warning for 2022.

0f7ff132baf7eda53163a89c4f74e547b72caa71.summary: Broadcom's protection bulletin describes Bofamet, a new Python-based infostealer found in the wild. From compromised endpoints it collects credentials, system information, browser cookies, Telegram session data, Discord tokens, screenshots and Steam configuration files. It exfiltrates this data to the attackers through a Telegram bot. The bulletin lists Symantec and Carbon Black detection names and recommends blocking malware execution.

0f7301a21c25468fd41c4eff0880dbf825b2664f.summary: Mandiant's May 2017 report attributes several 2017 incidents to FIN7, a financially motivated group active since 2015. FIN7 used application compatibility shim databases for persistence, patching services.exe to launch the CARBANAK backdoor, and also installed a payment card harvesting utility this way. The report describes the mechanism, names the sdbinst.exe tool, and gives detection recommendations.

0fd73fb19634637c9d66265f9b891826d8fffbea.summary: A 2019 security research write-up by Objective-See describes the author's search for dylib hijacking flaws in macOS apps and how it led to local privilege escalation to root. Writes to root-owned App Store app folders could be redirected during installation. The author used a benign-looking App Store app, Crontab Creator, as a proof of concept for root access through a cron job. Apple treated the installer issue as an enhancement, did not assign a CVE, and fixed it in Mojave 10.14.5. The author says a bypass of that fix followed.
